plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests three distinct structural strategies for a dichroic filter that transmits 1530-1565 nm while reflecting 400-700 nm, all within the 30-layer HfO2/SiO2 constraint. Route 1 explores a periodic quarter-wave Bragg stack centered on visible wavelengths, leveraging well-understood interference physics. Route 2 tests a chirped/thickness-graded approach to broaden the visible reflection band beyond what a fixed period can achieve. Route 3 introduces a defect cavity to create a transmission resonance specifically at the telecom band center. These axes are genuinely independent: a periodic stack may fail to cover the full 400-700 nm band, a chirped stack may sacrifice peak reflectance for bandwidth, and a cavity design may narrow the transmission window. Literature L01, L10, L11, L17, L23, L31, L35, and L38 inform material choice and optimization methodology, but no paper guarantees performance at these specific bands. All routes fix the material pair and layer count, varying only geometry.

routes.title: Periodic quarter-wave Bragg stack centered at 550 nm for visible reflection
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic quarter-wave stack with 15 HfO2/SiO2 pairs centered at 550 nm will achieve high reflectance across 400-700 nm while maintaining high transmittance at 1530-1565 nm, with performance improving as layer thicknesses are tuned from the ideal quarter-wave condition.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg reflectors create a photonic stopband centered at the design wavelength. By centering the stopband at 550 nm (middle of 400-700 nm), the 1530-1565 nm band falls well outside the stopband and should transmit. The HfO2/SiO2 index contrast provides sufficient reflectivity per interface.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (hfo2, sio2) repeated 15 times | sio2 substrate, total 30 layers
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 30 layers, initialized near quarter-wave at 550 nm
manufacturing_considerations: 30 layers is within typical ion-beam sputtering capability
HfO2/SiO2 is a standard low-stress pair for space optics
quarter-wave thicknesses are manufacturable with standard monitoring
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
HfO2/SiO2 dispersion data from measured datasets
expected_advantages: High index contrast yields strong reflection per pair
known_risks: Fixed period may not cover full 400-700 nm band evenly
Edge wavelengths (400 nm, 700 nm) may have lower reflectance
30 layers may accumulate stress or absorption losses
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 30-layer periodic multilayer coating on SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: alternating hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) layers, starting with hfo2, repeated 15 times for 30 total layers. Optimize individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Initialize thicknesses near quarter-wave condition at 550 nm center wavelength. Use measured refractive index data for hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from the material catalog. Total layer count fixed at 30.

routes.title: Chirped thickness stack to broaden visible reflection band
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A chirped multilayer stack with systematically varying layer thicknesses will achieve more uniform reflectance across 400-700 nm than a periodic stack, at the cost of slightly reduced peak reflectance, while maintaining transmission at 1530-1565 nm.
routes.design_principle: Chirped Bragg reflectors vary the optical thickness of layers across the stack, creating multiple overlapping stopbands that merge into a broader reflection band. By grading thickness from values appropriate for 400 nm at one end to 700 nm at the other, the full visible band can be covered.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | hfo2(1), sio2(1), hfo2(2), sio2(2), ..., hfo2(15), sio2(15) | sio2 substrate, total 30 layers with chirped thicknesses
design_variables: layer thicknesses with chirp parameter controlling thickness gradient across the 30 layers
soft_objectives: maximize minimum reflectance across 400-700 nm band
maintain smooth thickness progression to aid manufacturability
manufacturing_considerations: Chirped designs require precise thickness control per layer
Thickness gradient may increase deposition time
HfO2/SiO2 stress balance must be maintained across varying thicknesses
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method with non-periodic structures
expected_advantages: Broader reflection band than periodic stack
Better coverage at band edges (400 nm, 700 nm)
Thickness gradient provides additional optimization degrees of freedom
known_risks: Chirp may introduce transmission ripples in the 1530-1565 nm band
Optimization landscape may be more complex with chirp parameter
Manufacturing tolerance may be tighter for non-uniform thicknesses
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 30-layer chirped multilayer coating on SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: alternating hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) layers, starting with hfo2, for 30 total layers. Layer thicknesses follow a chirped progression where optical thickness varies systematically from layer 1 to layer 30 to cover 400-700 nm reflection band. Optimize the chirp parameter and individual layer thickness deviations to maximize reflectance uniformity in 400-700 nm and transmittance in 1530-1565 nm. Use measured refractive index data for hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from the material catalog. Total layer count fixed at 30.

routes.title: Defect-cavity stack with transmission resonance at 1550 nm
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Introducing a half-wave defect cavity layer within a Bragg stack will create a narrow transmission resonance at 1550 nm center wavelength, achieving higher peak transmittance in 1530-1565 nm than a simple periodic stack, while maintaining visible reflection.
routes.design_principle: Defect modes in photonic crystals create localized states within the stopband. By placing a half-wave cavity (optical thickness = λ/2 at 1550 nm) within a Bragg reflector, a transmission peak appears at the cavity wavelength while the surrounding layers maintain visible reflection.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (hfo2, sio2) x 7 | hfo2(cavity) | (sio2, hfo2) x 7 | sio2 substrate, total 30 layers with one defect layer
design_variables: Bragg pair thicknesses for visible reflection
defect cavity layer thickness for 1550 nm resonance
number of pairs on each side of cavity
soft_objectives: minimize transmission bandwidth to isolate quantum signal
manufacturing_considerations: Defect layer thickness must be controlled to sub-nm precision
Symmetry around cavity affects resonance quality
30 layers total limits the number of Bragg pairs on each side
theory_basis: Defect mode theory in photonic crystals
Transfer matrix method with defect layers
expected_advantages: Higher peak transmittance at target wavelength than broadband designs
Narrow transmission band reduces background noise
known_risks: Narrow transmission may miss parts of 1530-1565 nm band
Defect layer adds complexity to optimization
Visible reflection may be reduced due to fewer Bragg pairs
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 30-layer defect-cavity multilayer coating on SiO2 (Lemarchand) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: 7 pairs of hfo2/SiO2 (Lemarchand) Bragg reflector, followed by one hfo2 cavity layer at half-wave optical thickness for 1550 nm, followed by 7 pairs of SiO2 (Lemarchand)/hfo2 Bragg reflector (reverse order for symmetry), totaling 30 layers. Optimize Bragg pair thicknesses for 400-700 nm reflection and cavity layer thickness for 1550 nm transmission resonance. Use measured refractive index data for hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from the material catalog. Total layer count fixed at 30.

routes.title: Quarter-wave dichroic longpass stack tuned for visible rejection and telecom transmission
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 30-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave stack centered at 550 nm will produce a high-reflection stopband covering 400-700 nm while transmitting 1530-1565 nm, and individual layer thickness tuning can improve the balance between the two bands without exceeding the 30-layer constraint.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create high reflectance when optical thickness (n×d) equals λ/4 at the design wavelength. The reflection bandwidth scales with the index contrast ratio (nH/nL). Wavelengths significantly longer than the quarter-wave center see reduced optical thickness and transmit. Starting with high-index at the air interface maximizes front-surface reflection contribution.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | fused_silica substrate
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness condition: n×d = λ/4 creates constructive interference for reflected waves at design wavelength
Reflection bandwidth of periodic stack scales with index contrast ratio nH/nL - HfO2/SiO2 provides approximately 1.4:1 contrast in visible
Longpass behavior emerges when quarter-wave center is positioned below the transmission band - wavelengths 2-3× the center wavelength see sub-quarter-wave optical thickness and transmit
Starting stack with high-index layer at air interface increases first-interface Fresnel reflection contribution
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is manufacturable and well-understood in coating practice
30 layers provides sufficient pairs for high visible reflectance while staying within constraint
Thickness tuning allows optimization of edge position between 700 nm and 1530 nm
known_risks: Fused silica substrate name may not resolve - guaranteed_names lists sio2 but substrate may need fused_silica or quartz; this requires catalog lookup to confirm
Refractive index dispersion for HfO2 recalled as ~2.0-2.1 in visible, ~1.9 in near-IR but exact values from dataset may differ and affect quarter-wave calculation
SiO2 index recalled as ~1.45-1.46 across both bands but dispersion slope uncertain
Stress and adhesion for 30-layer stack not modelled - may require lookup of deposition process limits
No angle specified in request - assumed normal incidence but satellite application may have angular spread; this is a hypothesis
Edge steepness between 700 nm and 1530 nm may not be sufficient with simple periodic stack - may need chirp or matching layers not included in this topology
routes.execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer dielectric coating with air incidence on fused_silica substrate. Use exactly 30 layers alternating hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand), starting with hfo2 at the air side. Optimize individual layer thicknesses and the reference quarter-wave center wavelength to maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and maximize reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Normal incidence assumed. Both polarization states present but unpolarized weighting. Total layer count fixed at 30. Material names: hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), fused_silica.

research_influence: L01 informed the short-wave-pass filter concept for spectral separation, applied to all three routes
L10 provided dichroic beam splitter design principles, influencing the dual-band objective in all routes
L11 and L17 confirmed HfO2/SiO2 as a viable material pair for space optics, used in all routes
L23 informed optical constant selection methodology for HfO2-SiO2 systems
L31 and L35 provided laser damage threshold context for space-based high-power considerations
L38 influenced the needle optimization approach mentioned in route_01 and route_02 design variables
L02 and L19 informed the cavity resonance concept for route_03
L15 supported the use of advanced optimization methods across all routes
unresolved_decisions: Incidence angle not specified in user request; all routes assume normal incidence (0 degrees) as default for space-based receiver windows
Polarization state not specified; all routes assume unpolarized light or treat TE and TM equally at normal incidence
No numeric performance targets provided; routes use soft objectives for ranking rather than pass/fail gates
Substrate is specified as fused silica; using sio2 from guaranteed_names as the registry-resolved material
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all three routes fail to achieve best_target_score above 0.5 after maximum iterations, the problem may require relaxing the 30-layer constraint, adding additional material options beyond HfO2/SiO2, or accepting trade-offs between the two wavelength bands that cannot be simultaneously optimized with dielectric multilayers alone.

errors: This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone. No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied -- neither for the initial plan nor for any continuation round. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.

catalog.coverage: the guaranteed-name list proves name resolution only; the separate route candidate ranking reads actual n/k grids and records native coverage or explicit interpolation/endpoint-extension availability. Execution still keeps the registry's allow_extrapolation switch fail-closed

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

routes.title: Quarter-wave dichroic longpass stack tuned for visible rejection and telecom transmission
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 30-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave stack centered at 550 nm will produce a high-reflection stopband covering 400-700 nm while transmitting 1530-1565 nm, and individual layer thickness tuning can improve the balance between the two bands without exceeding the 30-layer constraint.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stacks create high reflectance when optical thickness (n×d) equals λ/4 at the design wavelength. The reflection bandwidth scales with the index contrast ratio (nH/nL). Wavelengths significantly longer than the quarter-wave center see reduced optical thickness and transmit. Starting with high-index at the air interface maximizes front-surface reflection contribution.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | fused_silica substrate
theory_basis: Quarter-wave optical thickness condition: n×d = λ/4 creates constructive interference for reflected waves at design wavelength
Reflection bandwidth of periodic stack scales with index contrast ratio nH/nL - HfO2/SiO2 provides approximately 1.4:1 contrast in visible
Longpass behavior emerges when quarter-wave center is positioned below the transmission band - wavelengths 2-3× the center wavelength see sub-quarter-wave optical thickness and transmit
Starting stack with high-index layer at air interface increases first-interface Fresnel reflection contribution
expected_advantages: Simple periodic topology is manufacturable and well-understood in coating practice
30 layers provides sufficient pairs for high visible reflectance while staying within constraint
Thickness tuning allows optimization of edge position between 700 nm and 1530 nm
known_risks: Fused silica substrate name may not resolve - guaranteed_names lists sio2 but substrate may need fused_silica or quartz; this requires catalog lookup to confirm
Refractive index dispersion for HfO2 recalled as ~2.0-2.1 in visible, ~1.9 in near-IR but exact values from dataset may differ and affect quarter-wave calculation
SiO2 index recalled as ~1.45-1.46 across both bands but dispersion slope uncertain
Stress and adhesion for 30-layer stack not modelled - may require lookup of deposition process limits
No angle specified in request - assumed normal incidence but satellite application may have angular spread; this is a hypothesis
Edge steepness between 700 nm and 1530 nm may not be sufficient with simple periodic stack - may need chirp or matching layers not included in this topology
routes.execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer dielectric coating with air incidence on fused_silica substrate. Use exactly 30 layers alternating hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand), starting with hfo2 at the air side. Optimize individual layer thicknesses and the reference quarter-wave center wavelength to maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and maximize reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Normal incidence assumed. Both polarization states present but unpolarized weighting. Total layer count fixed at 30. Material names: hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), fused_silica.
